construct: C1 inhibitor restrains plasma kallikrein and factor XIIa in the contact system. In hereditary angioedema caused by SERPING1-related C1-inhibitor deficiency or dysfunction, excessive kallikrein activity increases bradykinin generation, producing recurrent nonpruritic angioedema and abdominal attacks without urticaria.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: A young patient with recurrent nonpruritic angioedema and abdominal attacks, an affected parent, low C4, reduced C1-inhibitor function, and normal C1q has hereditary C1-inhibitor-associated angioedema.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Acquired C1-inhibitor deficiency can also cause low C4 and reduced C1-inhibitor function, but it generally lacks an autosomal-dominant family pattern, presents later, and commonly lowers C1q.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The age, affected father, absence of urticaria, normal C1q, and bradykinin-pattern attacks make hereditary angioedema the single best diagnosis.
